summary: I sent the exact prompt from the story. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec and every file under src/, test/ and src/ui/, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (428 lines). The page code in the plan imports dataTable, selectField, filterBar, statusChip, emptyState and pageHeader from '../ui/index.js'. It writes no hand-made <table> or <select> markup. No tracked file changed. The agent asked no clarifying questions.
reasoning: All four criteria pass based on the session log, the plan file and git status. The page code in the plan builds both the table and the environment filter by calling the library's dataTable and selectField. The agent also said it chose not to copy the Services page's hand-written markup.

observations.description: On first launch, the workspace-trust and Bypass Permissions dialogs both had "No, exit" selected by default. Pressing Enter there would have quit; I had to press Down first. This is harness or onboarding friction, not part of the product being tested.

To check the plan, the agent pasted its code blocks into a temporary copy of the repo (`mktemp -d`, `git archive HEAD`, extracted with a Python script) and ran `npm test`. It reported that all 35 tests passed. That is a nice check, but it means the agent ran code even though the user only asked for a plan. It stayed out of the working tree. Worth deciding whether this is wanted.

The agent said codex-plugin-cc isn't installed, so the plan only got its own self-review. It recorded this with the plugin's ungated-ledger script (degraded-gate, not-installed). It also said Task 2's "low" risk tier will be treated as standard. These notes about internal process may confuse a user who only asked for a plan.
The agent said it did not commit the plan because docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored in this repo. That is accurate and clearly explained.

The plan lists the choices the spec left open so the user can overrule them: Service sort defaults to A→Z, ties stay newest first, Started shows the raw ISO timestamp, the empty-snapshot message, and long durations stay in minutes. Good practice.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".
`wc -l` returned "428 docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md". The agent said: "The plan is saved at docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md".

criteria.criterion: Plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField (no hand-written <table>/<select>)
criteria.evidence: The src/pages/deploys.js code block in the plan has `import { dataTable, emptyState, filterBar, pageHeader, selectField, statusChip } from '../ui/index.js';`, `filterBar({ action: '/deploys', fields: [ selectField({ name: 'env', ...`, and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort: { key: sort, dir }, sortHref: ...`. I grepped the plan for `<table` and `<select`. The only hits are test assertions: line 158 `assert.match(html, /<select name="env" class="ui-select" data-autosubmit>/)`, which checks the library's output, and line 200 `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`.

criteria.criterion: No source/test/data/public files created or changed
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --ignored` printed only "!! docs/" (docs/ is gitignored). `git diff --stat HEAD` printed nothing. `find docs -type f` lists only the spec and the new plan. The agent ran the plan's code in a throwaway copy made with `mktemp -d` and `git archive HEAD`, not in the repo.
